items.title: Netscape shares reach $75 on day one
items.summary: The stock touched $75 on its first day of trading, a near record, and became the model for internet listings.

items.title: Telecoms Act signed into law
items.summary: The first big rewrite of US telecoms law in 60 years was signed on 8 February 1996, letting phone and cable firms compete.

items.title: Lucent becomes a separate company
items.summary: AT&T split off its equipment arm, which included Bell Labs, on 30 September 1996 as Lucent Technologies.

items.title: Greenspan asks about irrational exuberance
items.summary: The Federal Reserve chairman asked how we know when irrational exuberance has pushed asset values too high.

items.title: Amazon sells shares at $18 each
items.summary: Amazon, an online bookseller, offered 3 million shares at $18 each in its first public sale.

items.title: theGlobe.com posts the biggest first day
items.summary: theGlobe.com listed on 13 November 1998 and posted the largest first-day gain of any IPO up to that date.

items.title: Yahoo buys GeoCities
items.summary: Yahoo acquired GeoCities on 28 January 1999, when the free web-hosting site was the third most visited on the web.

items.title: JDS Fitel and Uniphase agree to merge
items.summary: JDS Fitel and Uniphase, two makers of optical parts, agreed to combine as JDS Uniphase.

items.title: WorldCom worth $180bn
items.summary: WorldCom reached a market value of $180.01bn on 21 June 1999, before its long slide.

items.title: Lucent worth $264bn at its peak
items.summary: Lucent reached a market value of $264.50bn on 9 December 1999.

items.title: Qualcomm shares rise 2,619% in 1999
items.summary: In 1999 Qualcomm shares rose 2,619% and the Nasdaq 85.6%, even though more stocks fell than rose.

items.title: AOL agrees to merge with Time Warner
items.summary: AOL, worth about $164bn, agreed to buy Time Warner, worth about $83bn, in an all-share deal announced on 10 January 2000.

items.title: Seventeen dot-coms buy Super Bowl ads
items.summary: Seventeen internet companies bought Super Bowl ads in 2000, at up to $2.2m for 30 seconds; a year later three did.

items.title: Global Crossing worth $49bn
items.summary: Global Crossing reached a market value of $49.12bn on 16 February 2000.

items.title: Nasdaq peaks at 5,048.62
items.summary: The Nasdaq Composite closed at 5,048.62 on 10 March 2000, the top of the boom.

items.title: Japan recession news sparks a sell-off
items.summary: News that Japan had slipped back into recession set off a global sell-off that hit technology shares hardest.

items.title: Barron magazine warns of burning cash
items.summary: The Barron cover story Burning Up said internet companies were running out of cash, and investors began to rethink.

items.title: MicroStrategy restates its revenue
items.summary: MicroStrategy announced a revenue restatement and the shares fell 62% in a single day.

items.title: Cisco briefly the most valuable company
items.summary: Cisco shares reached $82, valuing the company at $569bn and briefly putting it ahead of Microsoft.

items.title: Judge rules Microsoft broke antitrust law
items.summary: A US judge found Microsoft had abused its monopoly; the shares fell 15% in a day and the Nasdaq 8%.

items.title: Nasdaq falls 9% in one day
items.summary: The Nasdaq fell 9% on 14 April 2000, ending a week in which it lost 25%.

items.title: Qwest worth $90bn
items.summary: Qwest reached a market value of $89.68bn on 8 August 2000.

items.title: Enron worth $67bn
items.summary: Enron reached a market value of $67.05bn on 23 August 2000.

items.title: Sun worth $205bn at its peak
items.summary: Sun Microsystems reached a market value of $205.14bn on 1 September 2000.

items.title: Pets.com goes out of business
items.summary: Pets.com, backed by Amazon and known for its sock puppet ads, shut nine months after its listing.

items.title: Lucent warning drags telecoms shares down
items.summary: Lucent warned of a far bigger loss than expected; the shares fell nearly 20% and had lost 80% in 2000.

items.title: Cisco warns as unsold kit piles up
items.summary: Cisco warned sales would fall, took a $4bn charge, cut a fifth of its jobs and was worth under $100bn.

items.title: JDS Uniphase posts a $50.6bn loss
items.summary: JDS Uniphase lost $50.6bn in the year to June after writing down acquisitions, and planned 16,000 job cuts.

items.title: Attacks speed the market fall
items.summary: The 11 September attacks deepened the stock market decline that had begun in 2000.

items.title: Nortel cuts 20,000 more jobs
items.summary: Nortel warned of a $3.6bn quarterly loss, cut 20,000 jobs and named Frank Dunn chief executive.

items.title: Enron files for bankruptcy
items.summary: Enron filed for bankruptcy on 2 December 2001, then the largest in US history, after fraud was revealed.

items.title: Global Crossing files for bankruptcy
items.summary: Global Crossing filed for Chapter 11 with $22.4bn of assets and $12.4bn of debts; the shares had fallen 96% in a year.

items.title: WorldCom files the biggest bankruptcy
items.summary: WorldCom entered Chapter 11 with $104bn of assets, a month after admitting accounting fraud.

items.title: Nasdaq at its low, down 78%
items.summary: By 9 October 2002 the Nasdaq had fallen 78% from its peak and stocks had lost $5tn of value.
